hooks.text: A moon of solid rock stretches 300 feet every 42 hours.
What stretches a solid moon by 300 feet every two days?
Solid rock on Jupiter's moon bends like rubber hundreds of feet high.

title: The Moon Squeezed Until It Explodes
description: Jupiter and neighboring moons flex Io by hundreds of feet every orbit, fueling hundreds of active volcanoes that blast sulfur into space.

beats.text: A moon of solid rock stretches 300 feet every 42 hours.
beats.visual: Global color mosaic of Jupiter's volcanic moon Io, Galileo spacecraft, 1999

beats.text: Jupiter's moon Io is locked in a gravitational tug-of-war between the giant planet and neighboring worlds Europa and Ganymede.
beats.visual: Diagram illustrating the orbital resonance of Jupiter's moons Io, Europa, and Ganymede
queries: Laplace resonance Io Europa Ganymede diagram

beats.text: This orbital resonance generates enough internal friction to power roughly 400 active volcanoes.
beats.visual: Infrared view of active volcanic hotspots across Io's surface, Juno spacecraft, 2024

beats.text: Massive plumes blast sulfur and sulfur dioxide up to 300 miles into space at speeds exceeding 2,000 miles per hour.
beats.visual: Huge volcanic plume erupting from the Tvashtar volcano on Io, New Horizons, 2007

beats.text: This non-stop activity rapidly buries and erases impact craters, constantly repaving the moon's entire surface.
beats.visual: High-resolution view of Prometheus volcano and lava flows on Io, Galileo spacecraft, 2000

beats.text: These escaping ions power a massive electric circuit, burning a permanent glowing footprint into Jupiter's aurora.
beats.visual: Hubble ultraviolet image showing Io's glowing footprint inside Jupiter's polar aurora, 2000

beats.text: Every orbit, Jupiter and its moons continue to flex the rocky core of this terrifying world.
beats.visual: Linda Morabito discovery image of the Pele volcanic plume along Io's limb, Voyager 1, 1979

beats.text: It stays a volcanic nightmare because the giant planet's gravity never stops squeezing.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of Jupiter's gravity causing tidal heating in Io's rocky interior

better_than_last: Refined Beat 6 to incorporate specific reviewer feedback regarding the auroral footprint and ensured the loop flows perfectly back to the physical stretching described in the hook.
